sentences.text: This review covers the Volve development wellbore 15/9-F-14 in the Norwegian North Sea, written from general knowledge of the field without access to the daily drilling reports, survey data or casing records for this well.
No depths, dates, durations, hole sizes, volumes or rates are stated here, because they could not be checked against the source data.
Figures for hole sections, lost time, depth progression and fluid volumes should be taken from the field database and the final well summary before this review is relied on.
The well was drilled in the usual Volve sequence of surface, intermediate and reservoir sections, each isolated by casing before the next section was drilled.
The section-by-section hole sizes, casing shoe depths and new hole drilled per section need to be confirmed against the well's casing and survey records.

Drilling performance review should compare actual section durations with the planned times, and separate productive drilling from non-productive time such as equipment repairs, waiting on weather and downhole problems.
The primary and possible lost-time categories for this well should be extracted from the activity coding before any conclusion about the causes of delay is drawn.
Rate of penetration by section should be reviewed against offset wells in the same reservoir compartment to identify where the well performed above or below expectation.
Any lessons for future Volve wells should be tied to specific reported events, such as tight hole, stuck pipe, losses or casing running problems, and not to general impressions.
Completion and handover status should be confirmed from the well's final completion record before the review is closed.
